summary: Morocco's Foreign Ministry lists the nationalities exempt from an entry visa — including the US, the UK, France, Spain, Germany, Canada, Australia, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Russia and China — and its official eVisa portal (acces-maroc.ma) is open to citizens of a listed group of other countries, such as India, Thailand and Vietnam. The UK Foreign Office says the dirham is a closed, non-convertible currency that cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco.

currencyLimits.text: Moroccan Customs tolerates bringing in, or taking out, at most 2,000 MAD. safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says petty crime is common in tourist areas, especially in the medinas and on beaches: pickpocketing, bag-snatching and drive-by motorcycle theft. It says people posing as official tourist guides commonly harass tourists, and that a guide should have an official badge and permission from the local authority. It reports occasional violent crime, including knife attacks on tourists in major cities and along beaches, and advises avoiding quiet areas, particularly after dark. It says terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco, including in places visited by foreign nationals.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the Moroccan dirham is a closed, non-convertible currency. Moroccan Customs tolerates at most 2,000 MAD being carried in or out of Morocco. The Government of Canada says unused dirhams can be converted at the airport exchange counter on departure with proof of your initial currency purchase.

The UK Foreign Office says people posing as official tourist guides commonly harass tourists; if you use a guide in a medina, make sure they have an official badge and permission from the local authority. The Government of Canada advises hiring only official guides recommended by hotels, travel agencies or local tourist authorities.
The UK Foreign Office says that to fly a drone in Morocco you must get permission from the Directorate General for Civil Aviation, or you risk fines and confiscation of your equipment.

During Ramadan the Government of Canada advises refraining in public, between sunrise and sunset, from activities such as drinking, eating and smoking; the UK Foreign Office says doing so in public in the daytime may cause offence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Morocco?
faq.answer: No. Morocco's Foreign Ministry lists the United States among the countries whose nationals are exempt from an entry visa, but does not state how long the stay may last, and no official source we could read does. The UK Foreign Office says border officials should stamp your passport on entry, and that some travellers without an entry stamp have had difficulties leaving Morocco.

faq.question: How long can EU and UK citizens stay in Morocco?
faq.answer: UK citizens can stay visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism, according to the UK government; to stay longer they must request an extension at a Moroccan police station. EU citizens are also visa-exempt, but Morocco's Foreign Ministry list gives a stay length only for Hungary (90 days), and no other official source we could read states one.

faq.question: Can I buy Moroccan dirhams before my trip?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the dirham is a closed, non-convertible currency that cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco, and Moroccan Customs tolerates at most 2,000 MAD being carried in or out. The Government of Canada says unused dirhams can be converted at the airport exchange counter on departure with proof of your initial currency purchase.

faq.question: Who needs Morocco's eVisa and where do you apply?
faq.answer: Many passports, including several Latin American ones (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru), are on the Foreign Ministry's list of nationalities exempt from an entry visa. The eVisa is open to citizens of a listed group of countries — including India, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Brunei, Jordan, Israel, Benin and Guatemala — and to other visa-required travellers who hold a valid multiple-entry non-electronic visa from the US, Schengen, the UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Japan, Norway or New Zealand. Apply at the official portal acces-maroc.ma; its price list gives 3 to 7 days for the Standard track and 1 to 3 for Express.

Category C: Foreign citizens , subject to the formality of the visa, holders of one of the nonelectronic visas of countries which list is defined by the competent Moroccan authorities (Schengen, United States of America, Australia, United Kingdom, Ireland, Japan, Canada, Norway and New Zealand) holders of a regular passport valid for at least 90 days on the date of the application. This visa must be multiple -entries and valid for at least 90 days starting from the date of the electronic visa application.
The concerned citizens will have to make their requests via the link : www.acces-maroc.ma.

tips.closed-currency.text: The Moroccan dirham is a closed ‘non-convertible’ currency. This means it cannot be easily exchanged outside Morocco for other currencies
L’importation de dirhams est tolérée dans la limite d'un montant de 2.000 dirhams.
L'exportation du dirham est tolérée dans la limite d'un montant de 2000 dhs.
Unused dirhams can be converted at the airport exchange counter upon departure, with proof of your initial currency purchase.

tips.faux-guides.text: It is common for people posing as official tourist guides to harass tourists. If you use a guide in a historical district (medina quarter), make sure they have an official badge and permission from the local authority.
hire only official guides recommended by hotels, travel agencies or local tourist authorities

tips.drones.text: If you plan to bring a drone to Morocco, you must get permission from the Directorate General for Civil Aviation (in French) to fly a drone. If you do not, you risk fines and confiscation of your equipment.

entryRequirements.passportValidity.text: To enter Morocco, your passport must have an ‘expiry date’ at least 3 months after the date you arrive.
The Moroccan authorities have denied entry to some travellers with damaged passports.

entryRequirements.vaccinations.polio.text: To enter Morocco, you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had a polio vaccine if you’re coming from a polio-affected country.

countryFacts.safety.text: Petty crime is common in tourist areas, especially in historical districts (medina quarters) and on beaches. Crimes include: pickpocketing bag-snatching drive-by motorcycle theft of visible jewellery and handbags

It is common for people posing as official tourist guides to harass tourists. If you use a guide in a historical district (medina quarter), make sure they have an official badge and permission from the local authority.
There can be occasional violent crime in Morocco. Criminals have used knives against tourists in street attacks, thefts and burglaries in major cities and along beaches.
avoid quiet areas, particularly after dark
Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco.
Terrorism attacks could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy season usually extends from November to March, during which flash floods can occur frequently. These can be especially dangerous in the High Atlas valleys.

countryFacts.driving.text: You’ll need to have both the 1968 version of the international driving permit (IDP) and your UK driving licence with you in the car.
Morocco no longer accepts the 1949 version of the IDP.
If you stay longer than one year, you need a Moroccan driving licence.
